: Message from The YMCAs of Québec 


Strengthening the Foundations 
of fhe community: our premise 


2011 was a milestone year for The YMCAs of Québec as we celebrated our 160" anniversary. Since the 
opening of the very first YMCA in North America in Montréal on November 25, 1851, we have stayed 
true to our original mission which is to help all individuals achieve their full potential. 


We are reaffirming this promise with our current rebranding initiative, in collaboration with YMCA 
Canada. The harmonization of the YMCA brand across the country will allow us to improve the public's 
understanding of the scope of our community action, to expand our presence across the entire 
province and, we hope, to increase our capacity. It is this same objective that we are pursuing through 
our new communications plan, which confirms as our priority the development and well-being of 
Québec’s youth. In order to better meet their needs, an evaluation of the impact of the YMCA on the 
lives of the youth who participate in our programs and activities is currently underway. 


The celebration of our 160 years of existence reminds us that all of you - employees, volunteers, 
partners, donors, and members - play an essential role in the accomplishment of The YMCAs of 
Québec’s mission and, as a result, in the positive impact we have on our communities. We can 
take pride in a job well done over the course of the last 160 years and we look forward to another 
160 years of working together to build stronger and healthier communities. 


| 1 ft bis vod Highavr Valllacerul— 


Daniel Boisvert Stéphane Vaillancourt 
Chair of the Board of Directors President and CEO 


aceiiin ae andies Se eee 


“To be a partner of choice for volunteers, donors, and funders who wish to improve the well-being of children and youth 
in Québec.” Such is the commitment of the YMCAs of Québec Foundation, as manifested through its support of several 
initiatives implemented by the YMCA. 


This year, the Endowment Fund once again supported a dozen or so projects in accordance with this vision such as 
the Boot Camp weekend for girls at YMCA Camp Kanawana and the Drug Abuse Intervention program for youth at the 
Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA, as well as providing financial assistance to more than 300 disadvantaged children so that 
they can have an unforgettable experience in one of our day camps. As for the 26" edition of the Annual Golf 
Tournament and the Peace Medals benefit luncheon, these raised a record amount of funds which will be used to 
help even more young people achieve their full potential. 


These accomplishments would not have been possible without the generous participation and leadership of 

Michael Novak, the retiring President of the Foundation, who, in this role over the past eight years, helped build a 
strong Foundation for the future. We salute him for his 17 years of generous involvement with the YMCA. On behalf of 
the entire Board, we affirm our commitment to increasing the Foundation’s fundraising ability in order to continue 
to support YMCA projects, to ensure the sustainability of The YMCAs of Québec, and to secure the means for a 
positive impact for generations to come. 


Michael Goldbloom Laurent Giguére 
Chair of the Board of Directors President of the Foundation

THE ORGANIZATION’S 160™ ANNIVERSARY WAS 
CELEBRATED THROUGHOUT THE YEAR: 


We would like to thank you for being part of the history of the YMCA and 
for sharing our goal for the young and the not-so-young to be healthier and 
to achieve their potential. 


- As of June 18, friends of the YMCA were invited to travel back in time via 


historical displays featured in our 10 centres: the “160 Day Countdown” 
unveiled a new Y story every day until the anniversary date on 
November 25. 


On September 24, a party for donors and volunteers was held in the park 
of the Notre-Dame-de-Grace YMCA. More than 200 people gathered there 
to pay tribute to those who help us. 


November 24: the festivities drew to a close with a solemn declaration 
and the signing of the Livre d’or at Montréal’s Hotel de ville, in honour of 
the invaluable contributions of the YMCA to the Montréal community. 


November 25 and 26: birthday cake was shared in all of the YMCAs to 
celebrate with their communities. Of note, a plaque offered by Concordia 
University as well as a watercolour painting by Rosalie Williams - 

Sir George Williams’ great granddaughter, founder of the YMCA in 
London - were unveiled at the Downtown YMCA. 


“The City of Montréal is very proud to have been the 
location of the very first YMCA in North America. We 
can rely on The YMCAs of Québec which, year after 
year for 160 years, has been actively participating 
in the community life of the city. The organization's 
countless achievements and its positive impact 
on Montréal’s communities are immeasurable. 

We need only think of the recent opening of the 
Cartierville YMCA, which in only two years has 
become one of the cornerstones for the 

community life of the borough.” 


Jocelyn Ann Campbell, City of Montréal - 
Responsible for the Development of the 
Community, Families, and Seniors. 


Terry Finn, 99 years old and member for 85 years and his son 
Sean Finn, Executive Vice-President, Corporate Services and 
Chief Legal Officer at CN, and former member of the YMCAs of 
Québec Foundation’s Board of Directors.

MAKING AN IMPACT 


A new Camily at 
He YMCA 


They are named Maria Isabel, Hercilia, Patricia, Bertha, Clarisse, 
Martha, Paulina, Samantha, Gladys, Silvia, Angel... 


They come from all over the world: El Salvador, Colombia, Mexico, 
Saint-Vincent, Senegal, Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Algeria... 


They are fifteen women, refugees or asylum-seekers, whose ages 
range from 22 years to 83 years. They meet twice per week as part of 
the Women in Action group at the Residence’s PRAIDA-YMCA 

Day Centre. 


Together they share their artisanal know-how and culinary traditions. 


Together they share their thoughts and help each other in the 
resolution of their daily concerns. 
Together they share their stories. 


"Aqui, Todas so 


fae 


"Twit oroup allows us Te get out o€ fhe house and Feel better: 
Ip helps prevent depression and ménfal health problems, 
which weuld ofherwise come ata high cost te society,” 
claims Silvia, the group's advocate. 


A true "therapy," confirms Gladys. 


It is a respite for these women and, above all, for those who 
are mothers of young children for whom the nursery school 
lends a helping hand. Maria Isabel, mother of four children, 
enthusiastically mentions the family activities and the financial 
assistance that allowed her two eldest children to experience a 
stay at YMCA Camp Kanawana. 


These women, many of whom are seeking employment and who 
participate in the French conversation workshops, are the first 

to donate their time, talents, and gifts by volunteering with 

the Residence or other organizations working with the less fortunate. 
They even donate half of the proceeds generated from their 
creations — which are made with recycled materials — to the 

YMCA Strong Kids Campaign.

Kaitlynn is a 7-year-old student at St-John-Bosco school in Ville-Emard. Every day for the last 2 years, 
when the bell rings at 2:15 p.m., she boards the school bus and heads to the Pointe-Saint-Charles 
YMCA located close to her home. 


There, she is welcomed by Jennifer, Marcus, and Alex; animators with the Homework Help program. 


She finishes all of her homework by 4:00 p.m. and then takes advantage of the playtime and fitness 
activities right up until the time her parents arrive. 


In closing:

here, It's been very helptul since we are

A network of YMCA alumni 
A Mentors’ Circle for the YMCAs of 
Québec Foundation! Its raison d‘étre is to 
bring together former volunteers from 
the YMCA’s governance bodies who are 
dedicated to “being there to help the 
YMCA whenever needed’ in order to 
provide strategic advice, coaching, 
facilitate access to certain networks, 

and serve as ambassadors of the 

YMCA’s cause. The Mentors’ Circle is 
looking to expand! Do you know of 

any candidates? 


YMCA Peace Medals: 
25 years of distinction, 

86 laureates 

On November 18, more than 400 guests 
gathered to honour the laureates of 
the 25" Edition of the Peace Medals 
presented by Manulife Financial: 

Drew Steeves, from the Zero Force 
cycling team, Raoul Lincourt, 

President of the Centre de services de 
justice réparatrice, the Burgundy 

Urban Mediation Project, Equitas, 

and Dawson College. This year’s 
honorary laureate: Richard J. Renaud, 
accomplished businessman and 
philanthropist. Some $45,000 were 
raised to support our leadership 
development and social engagement 
initiatives for youth here and abroad. 


Corporate citizens, thank you for contributing to 

the educational success of our youth! 

Encouraging educational achievement for 450 children ages 6 to 12 in 
disadvantaged schools: such is the clear result of SNC-Lavalin’s 5-year $65,000 yearly 
investment into our Homework Help programs, which comes in addition to its 
investment for the provision of computer equipment to Ecole Jean-Baptiste Meilleur. 
Another exemplary partnership: “Adopt a School”, supported for five years by 
Desjardins Asset Management thanks to a $500,000 investment in a computer lab 
for Ecole Champlain, a Math, Science, and Technology resource centre at Ecole 
Marguerite-Bourgeoys, extra-curricular and enrichment activities, overnight stays at 
summer camp, and school bursaries. We would also like to thank: Caisse Desjardins 
des Versants du mont Royal, Fednav, Dectron Internationale, and Pomerleau Inc. for 
their support of various community initiatives.

Diversity, a youth leadership project 


Six youth leaders were selected to represent 
The YMCAs of Québec during the YMCA 
International Conference in San Francisco 
held from October 26 to 29, 2011, with the 
theme of “Building a Global Community 
Together.’ These six girls led several 
awareness activities and created a video 

in which various people expressed their 
thoughts on what diversity means to them. 
Fostering respect for people’s differences; 
such was the message they shared at the 
conference on behalf of Canada. Upon their 
return from San Francisco, they continued 
to be involved in solidarity projects. 

All different - All together! 


On your marks, set, ACTION! 

The YMCAs of Québec has implemented 

free leadership and international solidarity 
training for youth ages 16 to 25. This program 
encourages the citizen participation of youth 
through various projects such as You and Me 
Against AIDS, or Stop Child Trafficking, and 

a two-day training session on cooperation, 
communication, and engagement which 
was held on November 5 and 6, 2011. Events 
to look for in 2012: the TukTuk Show, which 
celebrates the artistic talents of YMCA youth, 
and the YMCA Youth Engagement Summit. 
Ready for action! 


Success through sports! 


Does the name Naismith mean anything to 
you? In 1891, in order to keep students busy 
during the winter months, a young James 
Naismith - then a gymnastics instructor at 

a YMCA in Massachusetts - was having fun 
creating a new game which was to become 
one of the most popular team sports in the 
world: basketball! What better way to 
channel our youth's abundant energy, 

have them work as a team, and surpass 
themselves! This is why this year Youth Zones 
from five YMCAs organized the Naismith Cup; 
a friendly basketball tournament. On 

May 6, 2011, youth from the Notre-Dame-de- 
Grace YMCA hoisted the trophy. An event for 
youth not to be missed!

COMMUNITY INITIATIVES 


AY for everyone! 


Thanks to the Access for All policy, in 2011, 6,139 people benefitted from financial assistance totalling $891,285 which is used to subsidise 
access to The YMCAs of Québec’s programs and facilities. The Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA created the “Projet de vie” membership which 


consists of a 75% discount for one year for people who are in the process of reintegrating in to the workplace. These individuals are referred by 
the centre's partners, notably organizations that provide social integration guidance, therapy, and shelter. In 2011, 50 people took advantage of 


this membership for a total of $5,645. A one-of-a-kind-opportunity! 


The YMCA comes to the aid of the homeless 

By raising awareness and through its work on the streets, the Dialogue support 
program for the homeless is aimed at identifying, supporting, and establishing 
contact with individuals in the Peter-McGill district who have no means, are isolated, 
and have no fixed address. This Downtown YMCA program, jointly founded in 1997 
with Destination Centre-Ville and Tandem Montréal, provides the homeless with the 
resources needed for them to regain control of their lives. Those who have overdue 
fines or criminal records are automatically referred to the YMCA’s Compensatory 
Work program or the Employment Service. Thanks to Dialogue, approximately 

20 homeless people every year are able to get off the street, which saves society 
some $400,000.

development programs! 


Urban agriculture, pilot projects 

On July 5, 2011, in partnership with the 
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA and C-Vert Mercier- 
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, the Tétreaultville and 
Maisonneuve-Longue-Pointe Eco-quartiers and 

the Y’a quelqu’un I‘aut’bord du mur organization 
inaugurated a brand new community garden in 
front of the YMCA called “Les Champs Olympiques” 
as part of the Paysage solidaire project. The garden's 
upkeep is a shared responsibility between youth 
from C-Vert, children from the YMCA’s day camp, 
and elderly volunteers. A great example of 
intergenerational cooperation! On August 26, it 
was the Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA’s turn to have its 
inauguration in order to offer children workshops on 
gardening and healthy eating. These gardens allow 
organic vegetables to be grown and help counter 
heat islands.

HEALTH, FITNESS AND RECREATION 


Healthy youth 

Because regular physical activity has a 
positive impact on youth, The YMCAs of 
Québec has implemented a Teen Policy for 
12-17 year-olds, who must participate in 
three orientation sessions in order to learn 
how to use our facilities safely. More than 
1,000 teens have participated in these 
sessions at the Cartierville YMCA alone. 
Equally successful have been the Friday 
Teen Nights, initiated by the West Island 
YMCA, which give neighbourhood youth 
access to our facilities free of charge or at 
a minimal cost. 


Taking action for the safety 

of our children 

In Québec, 25% of the approximately 

100 people who drown every year are 
children. With the success of a pilot project 
at the Westmount YMCA which offered free 
swimming lessons to elementary school 
children (of which 80% of the children lived 
below the poverty line) during class time 
over an 8-week period, and thanks to a 
major donation from CN, the program will 
be extended into other schools, allowing 
more lives to be saved. 


Working out at the YMCA, a responsible choice 
This fall, The YMCAs of Québec launched a new membership and active living awareness 


campaign: “Exercise change!” The campaign, which benefitted from the support of a televised 


public service announcement, demonstrated that by exercising at the YMCA, members are 
part of an organization that encourages youth in their endeavours, lends support to families, 


and comes to the aid of seniors. 


A brand new school! 


Renovations at the YMCA International Language School have allowed us to increase our 
capacity and therefore offer more groups, create new programs (German and Japanese) and 


welcome more students to our evening classes. 


Become a fitness trainer, national lifesaver, or first responder! 


Over 2,365 people obtained FIT certification, received additional training through health and 
fitness workshops, or learned how to save lives through cardiopulmonary resuscitation, first 


aid, or national lifesaver classes.

Getting involved for a better world! 


In February 2011, 52 people - including 

28 students - participated in The YMCAs of 
Québec / UNI-Alter delegation at the World 
Social Forum in Dakar in Senegal as part of a 
citizen engagement support project. Before 
their departure, the participants benefitted 
from approximately 20 hours of training. In 
Dakar, they participated in a day of discussion 
with youth leaders from the YMCA of 

Dakar and attended workshops with some 
70,000 participants and 1,200 organizations 
from 143 countries! 


a globa 


Y youth go international 


After a three-week preparatory session in 
Montréal, two young Canadians participated 
in a 5-month professional internship at the 
YMCA of Ecuador to support our partner's 
work with disadvantaged children, youth, and 
families who are mainly from Quito, but also 
from Portoviejo. The internship was funded 
by the Canadian International Development 
Agency as part of a three-year agreement 
which provided an opportunity for them to 
develop their abilities in organizing and 
facilitating workshops, as well as their 
communication and planning skills. 

A beneficial experience for all...

community 


YMCA of Haiti - Phase 2 

Sustained efforts by the staff and volunteers 
from the YMCA of Haiti, with the support of 
The YMCAs of Québec as well as YMCAs from 
the United States and Germany, have allowed 
the programming to be quickly resumed 

in three communities where the YMCA was 
present before the earthquake. A new centre 
was even built using converted containers. 

In 2011, over 2,000 youth and young adults 
were able to benefit from fitness activities, 
homework help programs, bursaries, or other.
